sections.title: QUAD ESL-63
sections.overview:
Released in 1981  430,000 (1 unit, around 1986)

QUAD spent a quarter of a century to complete the speaker system.This speaker consists of two fixed electrodes and a diaphragm placed between them.When a high voltage is applied to the vibrating membrane to generate static electricity and an audio signal is sent to the fixed electrode, a Coulomb force acts between the vibrating membrane and the fixed electrode to move the vibrating membrane and produce sound.This method does not require any strength because the diaphragm moves uniformly over the entire surface. It can be set to a very light diaphragm and can be driven with very little energy. It also has advantages such as good impedance matching with air and no need for a cabinet.The ESL-63 has succeeded in generating all frequencies at one point based on this system.Since a general electrostatic speaker is plane driven and tends to be plane wave, the listening position was limited.To solve this problem, in the ESL-63, the fixed electrode is divided into seven concentric rings and a delay circuit is set for each of them. By generating a signal delay of approximately 24 ? sec per stage from the inner circumference to the outer circumference, for a total of approximately 168 ? sec, we have succeeded in generating a spherical wave from a flat vibrating membrane. By this, the sound source is located approximately 30 cm behind the vibrating membrane and can freely respond to changes in directivity caused by changes in frequency.In addition to using a new material, Melinex, the manufacturing error is limited to   1/2dB compared to the reference machine. In order to realize high sound quality, it adheres to the QUAD policy.It has two built-in protection circuits to deal with unexpected accidents.It is equipped with a limiter that limits the input voltage and a circuit that detects abnormal input signals or momentary short circuits and does not send them to speakers.

sections.title: QUAD 405-2
sections.overview: Improved stereo power amplifier based on 405.The 405 / 2 is based on the 405 and has been improved to greatly increase the driving capability against load fluctuation.To solve the problems caused by the normal load line protection circuit, the QUAD has its own protection circuit, which smoothly reduces the abnormal current to within the safe operating range of the transistor and protects against short circuit. It is also integrated with the speaker protection circuit, which prevents the speaker from being destroyed by the trouble inside the amplifier.A current damping circuit developed by QUAD is adopted.This circuit consists of a single-output, small-power pure class A amplifier that amplifies voltage and supplies power for small signals, and a push-pull circuit with complete class B operation called a damper circuit. For small signals, current is supplied from the small-power pure class A amplifier to the load, and when the signal level increases, the damper circuit operates to supply a large current to the load.The low-power pure class A amplifier always detects and corrects errors between input and output signals and cancels all distortion at the output stage. In addition, it has low power loss, eliminates the need for idling adjustment, temperature compensation, and offset adjustment, and has excellent stability over time.

sections.title: QUAD FM4
sections.overview:
* Released in 1982  198,000 (around 1986)

Tuner for FM only.With QUAD's unique approach, it is designed to reproduce the input signal from the antenna with a rich musical quality without using techniques such as forcibly picking up weak radio waves.The front panel consists of an ON/OFF switch, tuning knob, push button for automatic / manual tuning, and graphic display.The graphic display shows the signal strength and tuning center as well as the frequency in digital form.The operating system utilizes the latest digital technology, and by adopting a microprocessor developed independently, it is possible to preset up to 7 stations.You can set a preset by first pressing the manual button to tune the desired station and then pressing the manual button and the button of the desired preset number simultaneously. The preset station is stored for approximately five years even after the AC power is turned off by the memory backup function.During manual tuning, AFC and muting are automatically disabled so that weak radio waves can be received.The best tuning point is when the two bar graph displays are at the same height.There was a wood case as an option sold separately.
